sentences.text: Hello everyone. Welcome to the everyday English podcast series. I'm Emily and
today we're going to learn how to speak English in a bookstore. A bookstore is
a wonderful place where you can discover new stories, learn new things, and find
the perfect book for yourself or as a gift. But what if you don't know how to
ask for a book in English? How do you find the right section? How do you ask
for recommendations or check for discounts? Don't worry. By the end of this episode
you will know how to ask for help, find books, ask about prices, order books, and
pay at the cashier in a bookstore, all in English. Let's get started.
1. Entering the bookstore and asking for help. When you enter a bookstore you may
want to browse freely, but sometimes you need help from the staff to find a book
or section. Useful English phrases for asking for help. Excuse me. Do you have
this book? Where can I find books about history, science, travel? Can you recommend
a good book? Do you have this book in stock? Where is the fiction nonfiction
children's section? Example dialogue. Excuse me. Do you have Harry Potter and the
Philosopher's Stone? Let me check. Yes, we have it in the fiction section. Great!
Where is the fiction section? It's on the second shelf to your right. Tip, if you
don't know the exact book title you can describe it by saying I am looking for a
book about space exploration. Can you recommend one? 2. Asking about prices and
discounts. If you find a book you like you may want to ask about the price or any
discounts. Useful phrases for prices and discounts. How much does this book cost? Is
there a discount on this book? Do you have any special offers? Do you offer
student discounts? Is there a sales section? Example dialogue. How much does
this book cost? It's $15.99. Is there a discount? Yes, we have a 10% discount for
students. Tip, some bookstores offer loyalty cards where you can collect
points and get future discounts. 3. Checking availability and ordering books.
Sometimes the book you want is out of stock. In this case you can ask to order
it or check if they have other additions. Useful phrases for checking
availability. Do you have this book in stock? Can I order this book? How long will
it take to arrive? Can I reserve a copy? Do you have this book in hardcover
paperback? Example dialogue. Do you have the great Gatsby in stock? Sorry, it's
currently sold out. Can I order a copy? Yes, we can order it for you. It will
arrive in five days. Tip, if you don't mind reading on a screen, you can ask, do
you have this book as an e-book? 4. Finding a book for a gift. Bookstores are
also great places to find gifts for friends and family. If you don't know what to
choose, you can ask the staff for recommendations. Useful phrases for buying
a book as a gift. I want to buy a book as a gift. Can you recommend one? Do you have
books for children, teenagers? Is there a special edition of this book? Do you
have books with illustrations? Can you gift wrap this book? Example dialogue. I want
to buy a book for my friend. Can you recommend one? Sure. What does your
friend like? Fiction, history, or maybe self-improvement books? He likes science
fiction. Then I recommend Dune by Frank Herbert. It's a great book. Tip, some
you have chosen your books. You need to go to the cashier to pay. Useful phrases
for paying. Can I pay by card? Do you accept cash? Can I get a receipt? Do you
have a return policy? Can I exchange this book if needed? Example dialogue. Can I
pay by card? Yes. We accept credit and debit cards. Great. Also, can you gift wrap
this book? Of course. It will take just a moment. Tip, keep your receipt in case you
want to return or exchange the book later. 6. Enjoying the bookstore experience. Many
new book. If you want to sit and enjoy a cup of coffee, here's what you can say.
Useful phrases for a bookstore cafe. Can I sit here and read? Do you have a
reading area? Can I buy a coffee and read my book here? Is this book available to
read before buying? Tip, some bookstores allow you to read before buying while
others prefer customers to buy the books first. That's it for today's episode. Now
you know how to speak English in a bookstore. We covered asking for help,
finding books, asking about prices and discounts, ordering a book, buying a book
as a gift, paying at the cashier, enjoying a bookstore cafe. Next time you
you in the next episode. Goodbye.
